title.value: A Unified Few-Shot Classification Benchmark to Compare Transfer and Meta Learning Approaches
title.justification: The paper presents a new benchmark, VTAB+MD, for comparing transfer and meta-learning approaches in few-shot classification.
title.quote: To bridge this gap, we introduce a few-shot classification evaluation protocol named VTAB+MD with the explicit goal of facilitating sharing of insights from each community.

analysis.description: The paper introduces an evaluation protocol called VTAB+MD that combines the Visual Task Adaptation Benchmark (VTAB) and Meta-Dataset (MD) to facilitate direct comparison between transfer learning and meta-learning approaches in few-shot classification. It conducts a large-scale study comparing state-of-the-art methods from both learning paradigms and provides insights on their strengths and limitations.

type.justification: The paper describes experimental results and comparisons between different few-shot learning methods using the VTAB+MD benchmark.
type.quote: We demonstrate its accessibility in practice by performing a cross-family study of the best transfer and meta learners which report on both a large-scale meta-learning benchmark (Meta-Dataset, MD), and a transfer learning benchmark (Visual Task Adaptation Benchmark, VTAB).

is_compared.quote: Few-shot classification benchmarks tend to standardize around a restricted set of input resolutions (84 ⇥ 84, 126 ⇥ 126) and network architectures (four-layer CNN, ResNet-18, etc.). Episodic training also imposes restric-tions on input resolution and network capacity, since the batch size is determined by an episode’s ways and shots and the support set cannot be trivially sharded into independent batches and distributed across multiple accelerators.
